what_happened: On a straight, busy highway, the policy's planned path (orange) bent left instead of following the route (green, and the command later turned RIGHT). The ego drifted left out of its lane, over the left edge and the concrete median barrier, and by 6.9s was going toward the opposite carriageway at about 5 m/s, 3.3 m off the human's recorded path. The camera view was clean before the drift and there was no conflict ahead that forced the move. The rear_ended flag doesn't match the rear-collision metric, which reads 0, and it played no part in the offroad failure.

The ego was queued in traffic behind actor 24, which was stopped or nearly stopped for the light ahead. The ego slowed from 2.0 to 0.4 m/s but never fully stopped, and it had drifted about 3 m left of the recorded path. It crept into the rear of 24 with its front corner at very low speed.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command (RIGHT by the last frame), the policy took over at 4.7s and its planned path swung left, away from the recorded trajectory. It cut across into the next lane to the left and side-swiped vehicle 41, which was moving alongside in that lane, at 6.2s. The lead vehicle stayed 15 m or more ahead the whole time, so braking for it was not the issue.

Moving at about 6 m/s in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane road, the policy planned a path (orange) that bent right, away from the route's straight-ahead path (green). The ego drove across the right edge line onto the dirt shoulder and was flagged offroad at 7.3s, 3.5 m from the recorded human path. The camera view was clean when the drift began, and no actor was close enough to force the move.

Although the route command was RIGHT, the policy steered left across several lanes toward the left road edge and sideswiped vehicle 32, which was holding its lane. The side collision came at 7.9s, about 11.6 m from the human trajectory, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

The route turned right (command changed from STRAIGHT to RIGHT, and the recorded path bears right). The ego instead held its line and drifted left while slowing from 19.7 to 11 m/s. It drove up onto the landscaped median island at 7.1 s, about 7 m off the recorded trajectory; no other actor was involved.

The route said STRAIGHT and the recorded path stayed in its lane, but after handoff the policy drifted right toward the next lane. It drove its front corner into vehicle 3, which was traveling alongside it in that lane. The lead car was still about 16 m ahead, so braking for the lead was not the issue.

Soon after handoff the policy steered left across several lanes, even though the route said STRAIGHT and then RIGHT and the recorded path stayed in its lane. Slowing from about 11 to 7 m/s, the ego hit actor 28 with its side on its left at 7.0 s, about 5.8 m off the recorded path.

The route said LEFT, but in slow highway traffic the ego steered right, away from its recorded path and its own lane, toward the lane where van 13 was ahead. It slowed from 4 to 1.9 m/s but still hit the van's rear-left corner with its front at 8.1 s, 2.7 m off the human trajectory. The rear contact flagged in the run came after this.
